page.layout: One printed page: a title block at the top, centred, with a woodcut frame ornament above it. Below the title, a paragraph of running text in one column, opened by a large woodcut initial D. Lines of Greek are set within the text. No margin notes. Signature "A" centred at the foot.

main_text.head: LEGES ATTICÆ
SAMVEL PETITVS
DE DEORVM CVLTV, SACRIS ÆDIBVS, diebus festis et ludis.
TITVLVS PRIMVS
main_text.p: DEORVM patria fuisse videntur Athenæ, siue illorum numerum spectes, siue Atheniensium [illegible, ~6 letters] quorum mita in Dijs colendis, præcæteris gentibus, religio: nam soli [illegible, ~5 letters] inquiunt ipsi apud Aristophanem Dii, &c. vtauctor est Xenophon in Lib. de Republica Atheniensium, [illegible, ~12 letters], ipsa ciuitas, [illegible, ~10 letters], [illegible, ~8 letters] ratione summa: atque id quidem ab antiquissimis temporibus, nam Triptolemi hæc Lex est:
Meminit huius Legis Porphyrius Lib. [illegible, ~30 letters], his verbis, [illegible, ~40 letters]

Idem è Xenocrate docet, siue potius à Porphyrio accepit B. Hieronymus Lib. aduersus Iouinianum II. Xenocrates, Philosophus de Triptolemi Legibus apud Atheniensis tria tantum præcepta in Templo Eleusinæ reliquere scribit: Honorandos parentes; Venerandos Deos: Carmina

page.notes: Greek lines are illegible at this scan resolution: the Greek in the second paragraph (after "hæc Lex est:") and the quotation from Porphyrius are not read letter by letter, so they are marked illegible. The Greek word after "siue Atheniensium" is also unreadable. The Latin words with [illegible] markers are blurred by the scan. The drop cap D is joined to "EORVM" as "DEORVM". No page number, running head, or catchword is visible. The last word "Carmina" stands at the end of the final line and continues onto the next page.
